content: Your doctor has prescribed ampicillin, an antibiotic, to treat your infection. This medication will either be injected into a large muscle, such as your buttock or hip, or administered intravenously through a needle or catheter placed in your vein. The intravenous infusion typically lasts about 30 minutes and is given four to six times a day. Ampicillin works by eliminating bacteria responsible for various infections, including pneumonia, meningitis, and infections of the urinary tract, gastrointestinal tract, skin, bones, joints, blood, and heart valves. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Your healthcare provider may monitor the effectiveness of your treatment and check for side effects using laboratory tests and physical examinations. It is crucial to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and the laboratory. The duration of your treatment will depend on how your infection and symptoms respond to the medication. Precautions Before Taking Ampicillin: Inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ampicillin, penicillin, cephalosporins, or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other antibiotics, allopurinol (Lopurin), anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin/Coumadin), atenolol (Tenormin), oral contraceptives, probenecid (Benemid), rifampin (Rifadin), sulfasalazine, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney or liver disease, allergies, asthma, blood disorders, colitis, stomach problems, or hay fever. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking ampicillin, contact your doctor immediately. If you have diabetes and regularly check your urine for sugar, use Clinistix or TesTape. Do not use Clinitest tablets, as ampicillin may cause false-positive results. Administering Your Medication: Before using ampicillin, inspect the solution carefully. It should be clear and free of floating particles. Gently squeeze the bag or examine the container to ensure there are no leaks. Do not use the solution if it is discolored, contains particles, or if the bag or container is leaking. Use a new solution and show the damaged one to your healthcare provider. It is essential to follow your medication instructions precisely. Do not stop your treatment prematurely, as this could worsen your infection and potentially lead to hospitalization. Do not alter your dosing schedule without consulting your healthcare provider. If you experience a mechanical issue, such as a blockage in the tubing, needle, or catheter, stop the infusion and contact your healthcare provider immediately to continue your therapy. Side Effects: Minor Side Effects: Ampicillin may cause mild side effects. Notify your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent: Upset stomach Diarrhea Vomiting Mild skin rash Severe Side Effects: If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your healthcare provider immediately: Severe skin rash Itching Hives Difficulty breathing or swallowing Wheezing Unusual bleeding or bruising Headache Dizziness Seizures Sore mouth or throat Storing Your Medication: If you are receiving ampicillin intravenously, you will likely be instructed to store it in the refrigerator or freezer. Remove your next dose from the refrigerator one hour before use and place it in a clean, dry area to allow it to reach room temperature. If additional ampicillin is stored in the freezer, transfer a 24-hour supply to the refrigerator for the next day’s use. Do not refreeze the medication. If you are receiving ampicillin intramuscularly, your healthcare provider will provide specific storage instructions. Store your medication only as directed. Ensure you understand the proper storage requirements. Keep your supplies in a clean, dry place when not in use, and store all medications and supplies out of reach of children. Your healthcare provider will instruct you on how to safely dispose of used needles, syringes, tubing, and containers to prevent accidental injury. In Case of Emergency or Overdose: If you suspect an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Signs of Infection: If you are receiving ampicillin intravenously or subcutaneously, be aware of the symptoms of a catheter-related infection, which occurs at the site where the needle enters your vein or skin.
